newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian senator quits key post.
newsitem.headline: Australian senator quits key post.

text.p: Key Australian independent senator Mal Colston, under police investigation over alleged abuse of travel allowances and shunned by political colleagues, on Tuesday quit the influential post of Senate deputy president.
But Colston will remain in parliament's upper house, where his vote with non-government parties can block government reforms.
"I have received a letter from senator Colston resigning as deputy president and chairman of committees," Senate President Margaret Reid told parliament.

The Queensland senator who quit the Labor opposition to sit as an independent last year has been under fire from all sides of politics to quit the deputy presidency over allegations he abused travel allowances. He denies any wrongdoing.
The Senate appointed Labor's Sue West to replace Colston.

The Liberal-National government, which has relied on Colston and another independent to pass crucial legislation, last month withdrew support for Colston as deputy president and said it would no longer accept his support.
But Colston said in newspaper interviews published on Tuesday he would now vote against all government measures.
